chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He is not one of us who breaks the trust.'
And he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Trustworthiness brings livelihood, and treachery brings poverty.'

key_terms.أَخْلَفَ: He broke / He failed to fulfill
key_terms.الْأَمَانَةُ: Trustworthiness / The quality of being entrusted

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and material consequence of being trustworthy or treacherous according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on entrustments, this hadith links spiritual identity to economic well-being, reflecting the Shia emphasis on al-amanah as a comprehensive moral virtue encompassing both divine and social contracts. The Prophet’s declaration that treachery invites poverty underscores the concept of barakah, where fidelity to trusts is seen as a direct cause of sustenance, a theme central to al-Kulayni’s ethical framework.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘He is not from us<sup>asws</sup>, the one who reneges with an entrustment’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The trustworthiness brings the livelihood and the betrayal brings the poverty’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy, who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘One who does not keep a trust safely is not of our people/
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Trustworthiness attracts wealth and treachery attracts poverty.’”
